q: Two documents of the Railways are sometimes confused with each other — one estimating the stores requirements of the year and the other listing the works approved for the year. The two documents are the Stores Budget and the Pink Book. Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: Both the documents list the works approved for inclusion in the Works Programme of the year
options.B: The Stores Budget lists the works approved for the year, whereas the Pink Book estimates the stores requirements of the consuming departments
options.C: The Stores Budget is a derived budget of the stores requirements of the Railways, framed on the basis of the requirements of the consuming departments and the programme of works, whereas the Pink Book is the Works Programme, listing the works approved for inclusion in the year, arranged Plan Head-wise with the provision made for them
options.D: The Stores Budget is voted by Parliament as a separate Demand, whereas the Pink Book is a register maintained in the stores depots

q: Advances for unforeseen expenditure are made both at the Union level and at the State level from contingency funds, and a probationer is asked how the two funds differ in their establishment and control. The two funds are the Contingency Fund of India and the Contingency Fund of a State. Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: Both the funds are established by laws made by Parliament under Article 267 of the Constitution
options.B: The Contingency Fund of India is established by a law made by Parliament and is placed at the disposal of the President, whereas the Contingency Fund of a State is established by a law made by the Legislature of the State and is placed at the disposal of the Governor
options.C: The Contingency Fund of India is placed at the disposal of the Governor, whereas the Contingency Fund of a State is placed at the disposal of the President
options.D: The Contingency Fund of a State is a part of the Contingency Fund of India, operated through the Reserve Bank of India

q: The revenue receipts of the Government of India are of two kinds, and a clerk preparing a statement of receipts is asked to distinguish between them. The two kinds are tax revenue and non-tax revenue. Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: Tax revenue consists of the dividends received from public sector undertakings, whereas non-tax revenue consists of the goods and services tax
options.B: Tax revenue is credited to the Public Account of India, whereas non-tax revenue is credited to the Contingency Fund of India
options.C: Both tax revenue and non-tax revenue are raised only through market borrowings
options.D: Tax revenue consists of the compulsory levies imposed by the Government, such as the taxes on income and the goods and services tax, whereas non-tax revenue consists of receipts such as interest on loans, dividends and profits from public sector undertakings, and fees and fines

q: Two financial officers of the Railways — one heading the accounts organisation of a zonal railway and the other sitting in the Railway Board — are sometimes confused with each other. The two officers are the Principal Financial Adviser of a zonal railway and the Financial Commissioner (Railways). Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: Both the officers function as the financial adviser to the General Manager of a zonal railway
options.B: The head of the Accounts Department of a zonal railway is a Member of the Railway Board, whereas the Financial Commissioner heads the accounts organisation of one zonal railway
options.C: The head of the Accounts Department of a zonal railway is appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, whereas the Financial Commissioner is elected by the Railway Board
options.D: The head of the Accounts Department of a zonal railway, the Principal Financial Adviser, heads the accounts organisation of the railway and functions as the financial adviser to its General Manager, whereas the Financial Commissioner (Railways) is a Member of the Railway Board and its principal financial adviser on matters of railway finance

q: In the accounts organisation of a railway, items held under objection during internal check are watched through one record, while the findings of a periodical inspection are communicated through another. The two records are the Objectionable Item Register and an inspection report. Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: Both the documents are reports issued by the statutory audit organisation of the Railways
options.B: The Objectionable Item Register is a register maintained in the Accounts Office in which items of expenditure or receipts held under objection during internal check, pending regularisation, are entered and watched till they are cleared, whereas an inspection report is the report by which the findings and objections of the periodical inspection of an accounts office or of the initial records of an executive office, carried out by the Accounts Department, are communicated to the office inspected
options.C: The Objectionable Item Register communicates the findings of an inspection, whereas an inspection report records the items held under objection during internal check
options.D: The Objectionable Item Register is maintained by the executive departments, whereas an inspection report is maintained by the Cash & Pay Office

q: A student of Government accounts is asked to bring out the difference between the Consolidated Fund of the Union and the Consolidated Fund of a State. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Consolidated Fund of India from the Consolidated Fund of a State?

options.A: Moneys can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of a State without any appropriation, whereas withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund of India require appropriation by Parliament
options.B: The Consolidated Fund of India is regulated by the Legislature of each State, whereas the Consolidated Fund of a State is regulated by Parliament
options.C: The Consolidated Fund of India receives all the revenues received and loans raised by the Government of India and moneys can be withdrawn from it only under appropriation made by law of Parliament, whereas the Consolidated Fund of a State receives the revenues and loans of that State and moneys can be withdrawn from it only under appropriation made by law of the Legislature of the State
options.D: Both the Funds are placed at the disposal of the President for meeting urgent unforeseen expenditure

q: To tide over temporary mismatches in its cash flow, the Government of India both takes advances from the Reserve Bank and issues short-term instruments in the market, and the two are sometimes confused. The two are Ways and Means Advances and Treasury Bills. Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: Ways and Means Advances are zero-coupon instruments issued in the market at a discount, whereas Treasury Bills are advances made by the Reserve Bank repayable within three months
options.B: Both Ways and Means Advances and Treasury Bills are advances made by the Reserve Bank of India to the Government
options.C: Ways and Means Advances are advances made by the Reserve Bank of India to meet temporary mismatches in the cash flow of the Government, repayable not later than three months from the date of the advance, whereas Treasury Bills are zero-coupon instruments issued at a discount and redeemed at face value, in maturities of 91, 182 and 364 days
options.D: Treasury Bills are repayable not later than three months from the date of issue, whereas Ways and Means Advances are issued in maturities of 91, 182 and 364 days

q: Two kinds of money come back to the Railways — fares and freight returned to the public, and amounts recovered from contractors who were overpaid — and a clerk asks how the two are treated differently in the accounts. The two are a refund of fares and freight granted to the public and a recovery of an amount overpaid to a contractor. Which of the following correctly distinguishes their treatment?

options.A: Both a refund of fares and a recovery of an overpayment are treated as revenue receipts of the Railways
options.B: A refund of fares and freight granted to the public is treated as a deduction from the earnings of the Railways, whereas a recovery of an amount overpaid is treated as a reduction of expenditure, by way of a deduct entry under the head of account originally debited
options.C: A refund of fares is treated as a reduction of expenditure, whereas a recovery of an overpayment is treated as a deduction from earnings
options.D: A refund of fares is charged to the Contingency Fund of India, whereas a recovery of an overpayment is credited to the Public Account of India

q: A comparative note is required on two articles of the Constitution — one dealing with taxes assigned wholly to the States and the other with taxes shared between the Union and the States. The two articles are Article 269 and Article 270. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the taxes referred to in them?

options.A: The taxes under Article 269 are levied and collected by the Union but are assigned wholly to the States, their proceeds not forming part of the Consolidated Fund of India, whereas the taxes under Article 270 are levied and collected by the Union and are shared between the Union and the States in the manner prescribed
options.B: The taxes under Article 269 are shared between the Union and the States, whereas the taxes under Article 270 are assigned wholly to the States
options.C: Both the taxes under Article 269 and those under Article 270 are levied, collected and retained wholly by the Union
options.D: The taxes under Article 270 are levied by the States and collected by the Union, whereas the taxes under Article 269 are levied and collected by the States themselves

q: An Accounts Assistant has to refer to the Indian Railway Accounts Code and is asked to state how its two volumes differ in their subject matter. Which of the following correctly distinguishes Volume I of the Indian Railway Accounts Code from Volume II of the Code?

options.A: Volume I deals with Traffic Accounts and station accounts, whereas Volume II deals with the general accounts of a railway
options.B: Both the volumes deal only with the classification of accounts contained in the Finance Code
options.C: Volume I deals with the purchase and custody of stores, whereas Volume II deals with workshop accounts
options.D: Volume I contains the rules relating to the general accounts of the Railways, including the maintenance of books and the rendering of the Account Current, whereas Volume II deals with Traffic Accounts, including station accounts and the Traffic Book

q: In the books of a railway, one record is the principal book of account and the other is only a list of balances extracted from it to test arithmetical accuracy. The two records are the Ledger and the Trial Balance. Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: The Trial Balance is the principal book of account, whereas the Ledger is extracted from it every month
options.B: Both the Ledger and the Trial Balance exhibit the assets and liabilities of the Railways
options.C: The Ledger is maintained by the executive departments, whereas the Trial Balance is maintained by the Audit Department
options.D: The Ledger is the principal book of account in which an account is maintained for every head of account, whereas the Trial Balance is the list of the balances extracted from the Ledger to test the arithmetical accuracy of the accounts

q: A question is raised how the Finance Accounts of the Railways come to be compiled by the Railway Board itself, while those of the other Ministries are compiled by the Controller General of Accounts. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the compilation of the Finance Accounts of the Railways from that of the other Ministries?

options.A: Both the Railways and the other Ministries compile their Finance Accounts through the Pay and Accounts Offices of the Controller General of Accounts
options.B: The Finance Accounts of the Railways are compiled by the Controller General of Accounts, whereas those of the other Ministries are compiled by the Railway Board
options.C: The Finance Accounts of the Railways are compiled by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, whereas those of the other Ministries are compiled by the Ministry of Finance
options.D: The consolidated Finance Accounts of the Railways are compiled by the Railway Board from the Account Currents rendered by the zonal railways and other accounting units, whereas the Finance Accounts of the Ministries whose accounts are compiled under the departmentalised system are compiled by the Controller General of Accounts

q: During the Budget debate in the Rajya Sabha, a member of that House proposes to move a cut motion against the Demand for Grants of the Ministry of Railways. The position under the Constitution and the rules of procedure is that:

options.A: A cut motion can be moved in the Rajya Sabha with the permission of its Chairman
options.B: A cut motion can be moved in the Rajya Sabha in respect of charged expenditure alone
options.C: Cut motions on the Demands for Grants can be moved only in the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha being able to discuss the Budget but having no power to vote on the Demands or to move cut motions on them
options.D: A cut motion moved in the Rajya Sabha has the same effect as one moved in the Lok Sabha

q: Two categories of Financial Bills are mentioned in the Constitution and in the rules of procedure, and a probationer is asked how they differ from each other in introduction and passing. The two categories are Financial Bills of the first category and Financial Bills of the second category. Which of the following correctly distinguishes them?

options.A: Both the categories of Financial Bills can be introduced in either House of Parliament without the recommendation of the President
options.B: A Financial Bill of the first category can be introduced in the Rajya Sabha, whereas a Financial Bill of the second category can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha
options.C: A Financial Bill of the first category, which contains any of the matters specified in Article 110(1) together with other matters, shall not be introduced except on the recommendation of the President and shall not be introduced in the Rajya Sabha, whereas a Financial Bill of the second category, which would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India but contains none of the matters specified in Article 110(1), can be introduced in either House, though it cannot be passed by either House unless the President has recommended its consideration
options.D: A Financial Bill of the second category is a Money Bill, whereas a Financial Bill of the first category is an ordinary Bill

q:
A probationer is asked to examine two statements made about 'Cash-in-Transit' in the railway accounts and to say which of them is correct.
1. Station earnings which have been remitted but have not yet been credited by the bank form a component of Cash-in-Transit.
2. Security deposits received from contractors, held under the 'Deposits' head, form a component of Cash-in-Transit.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A clerk who has seen the main Demands for Grants examined by the Standing Committees before voting asks whether the Supplementary Demands for Grants are also examined in the same way. In fact, Supplementary Demands for Grants are:

options.A: Examined by the Public Accounts Committee before they are voted
options.B: Voted only by the Rajya Sabha
options.C: Presented only during the Budget session of Parliament
options.D: Voted by the Lok Sabha without prior examination by the Departmentally Related Standing Committees

q: A Demand for Grant is put to vote in the Lok Sabha and is passed by the House. After it has been so passed, the Demand becomes:

options.A: An Appropriation
options.B: A Grant
options.C: A Vote on Account
options.D: A Budget Allotment

q:
Two statements are made about the passage of Money Bills under Article 109 of the Constitution, and a probationer is asked to examine them.
1. Article 109 of the Constitution lays down a special procedure for the passage of Money Bills in Parliament.
2. The Rajya Sabha may amend a Money Bill, and the Lok Sabha is bound to accept the amendments so made.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Two statements are made about the cheques issued by the Railways and their treatment when they remain uncashed for a long time.
1. A cheque issued by the Railways remains valid for payment for three months from the date of its issue.
2. A cheque which remains uncashed beyond its period of validity is treated as time-barred, and its amount is written back in the books through a transfer entry.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A probationer wants to know how the members of the Estimates Committee of Parliament come to be on the Committee. The members of the Committee are:

options.A: Elected by both Houses of Parliament sitting together
options.B: Nominated by the President for a term of five years
options.C: Appointed by the Speaker from amongst the members of the Rajya Sabha
options.D: Elected every year by the Lok Sabha from amongst its own members

q:
Consider the following statements about the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament:
1. The members of the Committee hold office for a term of one year.
2. The Chairman of the Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha from amongst the Lok Sabha members of the Committee.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A probationer is asked to state, besides the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States, one more subject on which the Finance Commission constituted under Article 280 makes recommendations.

options.A: The rate of dividend payable by the Railways to General Finances
options.B: The disinvestment programme of the Central Government
options.C: The borrowing limits of the public sector undertakings
options.D: The measures needed to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of the Panchayats and the Municipalities in the State

q: A historical note on railway finances records that the finances of the Railways were separated from the general finances of the Government of India under the Separation Convention of 1924. The Convention was given effect to through:

options.A: An Act of the British Parliament
options.B: The Government of India Act, 1935
options.C: A resolution adopted by the Legislative Assembly
options.D: A notification issued by the Railway Board

q: The management of a zonal railway does not wait for the final accounted earnings and obtains figures of the earnings of the railway at short intervals during the year from the station returns. These figures are the approximate earnings of the railway, compiled and reported at intervals of:

options.A: Every day
options.B: Every two months
options.C: Every quarter
options.D: Every ten days

q: For meeting urgent unforeseen expenditure, advances are made from a fund which the Constitution places at the disposal of one authority. That fund is the Contingency Fund of India, which is placed at the disposal of:

options.A: The President
options.B: The Finance Minister
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Prime Minister

q: A probationer examining the monthly account rendered by a zonal railway to the Railway Board asks what transactions that account covers. The Account Current comprises:

options.A: Both the cash transactions and the transfer (adjustment) transactions of the month
options.B: Only the cash transactions of the month
options.C: Only the transfer transactions of the month
options.D: Only the transactions relating to the Railway Board's own office

q: During the course of a financial year, the need for additional grants for the Railways arises more than once, and a clerk asks whether Supplementary Demands can be presented again. The correct position is that Supplementary Demands for Grants:

options.A: Can be presented only once during a financial year
options.B: Can be presented only in the Budget session of Parliament
options.C: Are presented only after the close of the financial year
options.D: May be presented more than once during a financial year, as and when the need arises

q: A zonal railway is waiting for the communication of its budget allotment for the financial year after the Budget has been passed by Parliament. Ordinarily, the budget allotment for a financial year is communicated by the Railway Board to the zonal railways:

options.A: After the Appropriation Act for the year has been passed
options.B: Before the presentation of the Budget in Parliament
options.C: Only at the Final Modification stage in January
options.D: Along with the Revised Estimates in September

q: A clerk assumes that every unit of the Railways, including a division and a large station, renders its own monthly Account Current to the Railway Board, and he is corrected with reference to one kind of unit which does so. The unit which renders its own monthly Account Current is:

options.A: A production unit, such as the Integral Coach Factory
options.B: A railway division
options.C: A large railway station
options.D: A sub-divisional engineering office

q: A clerk has to cite the authority which issues the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account (LMMH) followed by the Central and the State Governments. The List is issued by the:

options.A: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: Controller General of Accounts
options.C: Budget Division of the Ministry of Finance
options.D: Railway Board

q: A work has been included in the Works Programme but its detailed estimate is still awaited and the competent authority has not yet sanctioned it. What does the Budget provide for such a work?

options.A: The full estimated cost of the work
options.B: Only a token provision
options.C: A provision under Manufacturing Suspense
options.D: No provision, and the work is dropped from the Programme

q:
Consider the following statements about the January review of the Railway Budget:
1. At the Final Modification stage, the figures are worked out broadly with reference to the actuals of the first nine months of the year.
2. The object of the stage is to settle the Final Grant by surrendering foreseen savings and providing for additional requirements through re-appropriation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

q: Transactions of a zonal railway with a public sector bank are lying unsettled because the bank's advice has not been received. Through which suspense head are such transactions passed?

options.A: PSB Suspense
options.B: Reserve Bank Suspense
options.C: PAO Suspense
options.D: AG Suspense

q: Goods have been received and services rendered to a zonal railway by outside suppliers, but payment has not yet been made. Pending payment, the amount due by the railway is held under the head:

options.A: Demands Recoverable
options.B: Miscellaneous Advances
options.C: Demands Payable
options.D: Deposits

q: At the end of a month, the Accounts Office prepares a statement listing the debit and credit balances of all Ledger accounts in order to test whether total debits equal total credits. This statement is the:

options.A: Classified Abstract
options.B: Trial Balance
options.C: Debt Head Report
options.D: Account Current

q: A disbursing officer has made a number of small contingent payments during the month. What is the ordinary treatment of the sub-vouchers supporting such small payments?

options.A: They are forwarded to the Comptroller and Auditor General
options.B: They are destroyed as soon as the payment is made
options.C: They are published with the monthly accounts
options.D: They are retained by the disbursing officer in his office and not forwarded to the Accounts Office

q: The officer holding a permanent imprest is transferred to another post. Before handing over charge, he is required to:

options.A: Account for the imprest in full and hand over the balance to his successor
options.B: Retain the imprest until the successor claims it
options.C: Spend the unspent balance on office contingencies
options.D: Deposit the balance in the Public Account in his own name

q: Because a large number of adjustments accumulate at the close of the financial year, the monthly Account Current for March is not rendered as a single account. It is rendered in the two parts called:

options.A: March (Revenue) and March (Capital)
options.B: March (Voted) and March (Charged)
options.C: March (Preliminary) and March (Final)
options.D: March (Ordinary) and March (Supplementary)

q: Under exchequer control as now operated for Government departments, the pace of expenditure during the year is regulated through:

options.A: Budget proportions communicated in the Pink Book
options.B: Monthly Expenditure Plans and Quarterly Expenditure Plans
options.C: Re-appropriation statements rendered every month
options.D: The Appropriation Accounts of the previous year

q: In the Balance Sheet context, a debit balance standing under Stores Suspense (Plan Head 71) represents:

options.A: Stores purchased but not yet paid for
options.B: Stores issued to works but not yet adjusted
options.C: Amounts recoverable from suppliers
options.D: The value of stores held in stock in the stores depots

q: A workshop has several jobs on the shop floor on which labour, material and on-cost have been booked but which are not yet completed. The balance under Manufacturing Suspense represents:

options.A: The cost of jobs still in progress in the workshops
options.B: The value of finished products awaiting sale
options.C: Amounts due from other railways for jobs done for them
options.D: Depreciation accumulated on workshop plant

q: A transfer transaction between two zonal railways reaches the books of the Railway Board for final adjustment. In the Board's books it is adjusted under the head:

options.A: PAO Suspense
options.B: Reserve Bank Suspense
options.C: Transfer Railways
options.D: AG Suspense

q: A sum is payable by an outside party to a zonal railway for services rendered by the railway and is awaiting realisation. Pending realisation, the amount is debited to:

options.A: Miscellaneous Advances
options.B: Demands Recoverable
options.C: Deposits
options.D: Cheques and Bills

q: A zonal railway pays an advance to a party which is recoverable or adjustable in due course, the final head not being chargeable at once. Such an advance is initially held under:

options.A: Demands Recoverable
options.B: Deposits
options.C: Traffic Suspense
options.D: Miscellaneous Advances

q: Earnest money deposited by a contractor along with his tender is received by a zonal railway. Until it is refunded or forfeited, the money is held under:

options.A: The 'Deposits' head among the Debt heads
options.B: Sundry Other Earnings of the year
options.C: Capital receipts of the railway
options.D: Miscellaneous revenue receipts of the year

q: Deposits received by a railway remain unclaimed by the depositors for more than the period prescribed in the rules and are therefore treated as lapsed. The prescribed period after which deposits lapse to revenue is:

options.A: One year
options.B: Two years
options.C: Three years
options.D: Five years

q: While fixing the year's appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund, the Accounts Office works with reference to:

options.A: The original cost of the asset and its prescribed codal life
options.B: The current market value of the asset
options.C: The gross earnings of the year
options.D: The dividend liability of the Railways

q: The annual appropriation from revenue to the Railway Pension Fund is not fixed as a flat percentage of earnings. It is assessed with reference to:

options.A: The gross earnings of the year
options.B: The dividend liability of the Railways
options.C: The balance available in the Development Fund
options.D: The actuarial valuation of the pension liability

q: Unlike the Depreciation Reserve Fund, which is fed by a charge on working expenses, the Development Fund of the Railways is credited with appropriations made out of:

options.A: Gross Budgetary Support
options.B: The surplus of the Railways
options.C: Market borrowings through IRFC
options.D: The working expenses of the year

q: A fund was created in 1993-94 so that the Railways could finance capital works out of their own internal resources instead of depending wholly on budgetary support. That fund is the:

options.A: Development Fund
options.B: Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Capital Fund
options.D: Railway Safety Fund

q: The Special Railway Safety Fund set up in 2001-02 was provided with a corpus of:

options.A: Rs 17,000 crore
options.B: Rs 10,000 crore
options.C: Rs 20,000 crore
options.D: Rs 25,000 crore

q: The Special Railway Safety Fund was set up on the recommendations of:

options.A: The Railway Convention Committee
options.B: The Bibek Debroy Committee
options.C: The Rakesh Mohan Committee
options.D: The Railway Safety Review Committee (Khanna Committee)

q: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh draws its financing from:

options.A: A surcharge on passenger fares only
options.B: Gross Budgetary Support and the Railways' internal resources
options.C: Market borrowings through IRFC only
options.D: Fines and penalties collected by the Railways

q:
Consider the following statements about the Railway Safety Fund:
1. It is credited with the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares.
2. It also receives a share of the cess levied on petrol and diesel, through the Central Road Fund.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: In an allocation string such as 'DRF-3100', the element written before the Plan Head number indicates:

options.A: The source of finance from which the work is financed
options.B: The zonal railway executing the work
options.C: The year in which the work was sanctioned
options.D: The Primary Unit of the work

q: A passenger amenity work at a station is financed from the Development Fund and is classified under Plan Head 53. Its complete allocation is written as:

options.A: Capital-5300

q: Staff quarters are constructed as a labour welfare work and the cost is met from the Development Fund, the Plan Head for staff quarters being 51. The allocation of the work is:

options.A: Capital-5100

q: An existing asset is replaced by a materially heavier and better asset. The cost is apportioned between funds in which of the following ways?

options.A: The entire cost is charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.B: The entire cost is charged to Capital
options.C: The cost of the like-for-like element goes to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the additional cost of betterment to Capital/Development Fund
options.D: The entire cost is shared equally between the Depreciation Reserve Fund and Capital

q: A new line is still under construction and has not been opened for public traffic, but it earns some receipts during construction. Such net earnings, if any, before opening are:

options.A: Credited to the Capital account of the work, in reduction of its cost
options.B: Credited to the revenue earnings of the year
options.C: Credited to the Development Fund
options.D: Treated as Sundry Other Earnings

q: Interest is payable on capital borrowed for a work while the work is still under construction. This interest during construction is:

options.A: Charged to the working expenses of the year
options.B: Debited to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Ignored in the accounts until the work is completed
options.D: Treated as part of the cost of the work and charged to Capital

q: Land is acquired for a sanctioned railway work and its cost is paid. In the accounts of the work, the cost of the land is:

options.A: Treated as part of the capital cost of the work
options.B: Charged to the working expenses of the year of acquisition
options.C: Debited to the Development Fund in all cases
options.D: Kept permanently under a suspense head

q: Money is spent on surveys and investigations for a proposed project, but the project is ultimately abandoned and is not taken up for construction. The preliminary expenses so incurred are charged to:

options.A: The capital cost of the project
options.B: Revenue, as ordinary working expenses
options.C: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: The Development Fund

q: A work of small value, within the limit prescribed in the Finance Code for the purpose, is executed on the open line. Such a work may be charged to:

options.A: Capital
options.B: Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh
options.C: Ordinary revenue (working expenses)
options.D: Stores Suspense

q: Services such as general administration and supervision are common to both new construction and open-line working. The cost of such common services is allocated between Capital and Revenue:

options.A: Equally in all cases
options.B: Entirely to Revenue
options.C: Entirely to Capital
options.D: In the proportions prescribed in the rules/codes for such allocation

q: The Accounts Office uses the Works Register mainly to keep control over works expenditure by:

options.A: Recording the liabilities incurred under works contracts
options.B: Comparing the progressive expenditure on each sanctioned work with its sanctioned estimate, so that excesses over estimates are watched and regularised
options.C: Recording the attendance of the works staff
options.D: Showing the balances of stores issued to each work

q: The Liability Register maintained in the Accounts Office serves budgetary control by ensuring that:

options.A: The cash balance with the Reserve Bank is never overdrawn
options.B: The stores balances agree with the priced ledgers
options.C: The commitments and liabilities incurred against a grant do not exceed the budget allotment available for the purpose
options.D: The earnings of the railway agree with the Traffic Book

q: The Railway Board needs to amend the list of major, minor and other heads contained in the Finance Code. Such amendments and corrections to the classification of accounts are issued through:

options.A: Budget Circulars
options.B: Transfer Certificates
options.C: Entries in the Pink Book
options.D: Correction Slips

q: The detailed classification of railway accounts, listing the Major Heads, Sub-Major Heads, Minor Heads and Primary Units, is prescribed in:

options.A: Indian Railway Finance Code, Volume II
options.B: Indian Railway Accounts Code, Volume I
options.C: Indian Railway Stores Code
options.D: Indian Railway Finance Code, Volume I

q: Under E-Recon, the facility which the responding railway actually gains is:

options.A: Freedom from accepting a transfer transaction at all, since the advice is electronic
options.B: Online monitoring of transfer transactions which remain unmatched or unaccepted
options.C: Automatic write-off of unmatched transfers
options.D: Dispensing with the Debt Head Report

q:
Consider the following statements about the earnings of the Railways:
1. Earnings are brought to account on the basis of the traffic booked, irrespective of when the cash for it is collected.
2. Earnings are brought to account only when the cash is actually received at stations.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 2 only
options.B: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: In the Balance Sheet of the Railways, the accumulated balances of the Railway Funds, such as the Depreciation Reserve Fund, Development Fund and Pension Fund, are exhibited on:

options.A: The assets side
options.B: Neither side, as the funds are kept outside the Balance Sheet
options.C: The assets side only, as investments of the funds
options.D: The liabilities side

q: A particular line is maintained by the Railways purely for defence considerations and it runs at a working loss year after year. That working loss is ultimately borne by:

options.A: The Development Fund
options.B: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: The Capital Fund
options.D: General Revenues, which reimburse the Railways on strategic considerations

q: At the close of a month, station earnings have been remitted but have not yet been credited by the bank, and the amount stands as Cash-in-Transit. In the classification of accounts, Cash-in-Transit falls under the:

options.A: Revenue heads
options.B: Capital heads
options.C: Remittance heads
options.D: Debt heads

q: For linking the capital accounts of the Railways with the accounts of the Central Government, the Plan Heads function, under Major Heads 5002 and 5003, as the:

options.A: Sub-Major Heads
options.B: Detailed Heads
options.C: Minor Heads
options.D: Primary Units

q:
Consider the following statements about Sundry Other Earnings:
1. They are credited wholly to the railway on which they accrue and are not subject to apportionment.
2. They arise from carriage of traffic over more than one railway and are divided in proportion to distance.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The Accounts Office of a zonal railway receives, every day, a statement from the accredited bank listing the receipts credited and the payments made on the railway's behalf, and uses it to reconcile the bank's transactions with the railway books. This daily statement is known as the:

options.A: Classified Abstract
options.B: Bank Scroll
options.C: Account Current
options.D: Debt Head Report

q:
An Accounts clerk passes a transfer adjustment in the Journal Book without any supporting voucher, arguing that journal entries need no documentation. Consider the following statements in this context:
1. A journal entry has to be supported by a Journal Voucher signed by an Accounts Officer.
2. Journal Vouchers and cash vouchers run in a single common numbering series.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A clerk argues that a wrong booking of expenditure under an incorrect head of account will necessarily throw the Trial Balance of the railway out of agreement. The correct position is that such an error of classification:

options.A: Always prevents the Trial Balance from agreeing
options.B: Is brought to light automatically by the Trial Balance
options.C: Does not affect the agreement of the Trial Balance, since the total debits and total credits remain equal
options.D: Can be rectified only with the sanction of Parliament

q: A bill presented by an engineering executive for payment shows no allocation at all. The primary responsibility for showing the correct head of account on a bill or voucher rests with:

options.A: The Accounts Officer who passes the bill for payment
options.B: The Cash & Pay Office which makes the payment
options.C: The Railway Board
options.D: The executive (departmental) officer who presents the bill

q: A disbursing officer makes a number of small contingent payments and retains the supporting sub-vouchers in his own office instead of forwarding them to the Accounts Office. This practice is:

options.A: Correct, as sub-vouchers for small contingent payments are ordinarily retained by the disbursing officer and not forwarded to the Accounts Office
options.B: Incorrect, as every sub-voucher must be sent directly to the Comptroller and Auditor General
options.C: Incorrect, as the sub-vouchers must be destroyed immediately after payment
options.D: Incorrect, as the sub-vouchers must be published with the monthly accounts

q: An officer holding a permanent imprest is transferred to another post. Before handing over charge, he is required to:

options.A: Retain the imprest amount until his successor demands it
options.B: Spend the unspent balance before handing over charge
options.C: Account for the imprest in full and hand over the balance to his successor
options.D: Deposit the imprest balance in the Public Account in his own name

q: A Station Master proposes to meet the station's petty contingent expenses out of the day's earnings collections and remit only the balance. The correct position is that the earnings collected at a station are required to be:

options.A: Retained at the station till the close of the financial year
options.B: Remitted in full to the Cash Office or the accredited bank, and not utilised for local expenditure
options.C: Adjusted against the imprest held by the Station Master
options.D: Utilised first for contingent expenditure, with only the surplus remitted

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'earnings' from 'receipts' in railway accounts?

options.A: Earnings relate to goods traffic only, whereas receipts relate to all traffic
options.B: Earnings are accounted only in the books of the Railway Board, whereas receipts are accounted at the stations
options.C: Earnings are always smaller than receipts
options.D: Earnings represent the amounts earned for the services rendered, as brought to account from the station and traffic returns, whereas receipts represent the cash actually realised and remitted

q: While preparing the Detailed Demands for Grants, a clerk proposes to show the estimates net of all recoveries, without showing the recoveries anywhere. The correct position is that the estimates in the Detailed Demands for Grants are exhibited:

options.A: On a gross basis, the recoveries being shown separately as 'Deduct' entries to arrive at the net amount of the Demand
options.B: Only for the charged portion of the expenditure
options.C: Only in terms of the net cash outgo from the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: Net of all recoveries, the recoveries not being shown at all

q: A Member of Parliament objects that a Vote on Account granted by the Lok Sabha also authorises the Government's taxation proposals for part of the year. The correct position is that a Vote on Account:

options.A: Authorises the Government to levy taxes for a part of the financial year
options.B: Covers the estimates of receipts as well as of expenditure
options.C: Authorises withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India for meeting expenditure for a part of the financial year, pending completion of the budgetary process; it does not deal with the taxation proposals
options.D: Is required only when a new Government is formed after a general election

q:
Consider the following statements about the general discussion on the Budget in Parliament:
1. No discussion on the Budget takes place on the day on which it is presented.
2. During the general discussion which follows, no motion can be moved and no voting on the Demands for Grants takes place.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: At the Final Modification stage, a zonal railway surrenders the savings it anticipates out of its sanctioned grant. This surrender of anticipated savings:

options.A: Requires the vote of the Lok Sabha
options.B: Requires a Supplementary Demand for Grants
options.C: Can be made only after the Appropriation Accounts of the year are finalised
options.D: Is an executive act and does not require the approval of Parliament

q: Savings under one head of a grant are diverted to meet expenditure under another head of the same grant. Such re-appropriation of funds is effected:

options.A: By the competent executive authority under the powers delegated for the purpose, without the approval of Parliament
options.B: Only with the prior approval of Parliament
options.C: Only with the approval of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Only through a Supplementary Demand for Grant

q: A private member of the Lok Sabha wishes to introduce a Money Bill in the House. This is not permissible because a Money Bill can be introduced in the Lok Sabha only:

options.A: By any member authorised by the President
options.B: By the Chairman of the Estimates Committee
options.C: By a Minister, that is, it can only be a Government Bill
options.D: By a member of the Opposition nominated by the Speaker

q: A finance branch note claims that the working of the Contingency Fund of India, created under Article 267, is governed by the General Financial Rules. The instrument which actually regulates the Fund is:

options.A: The General Financial Rules
options.B: The Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950
options.C: The FRBM Act, 2003
options.D: The Appropriation Act of the year concerned

q: Under the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK), the assured annual outlay is Rs 20,000 crore. Of this annual outlay, the contribution made from Gross Budgetary Support is:

options.A: Rs 5,000 crore
options.B: Rs 10,000 crore
options.C: Rs 20,000 crore
options.D: Rs 15,000 crore

q: The Special Railway Safety Fund (SRSF) was closed in the year 2008. On its closure, the unspent balance of the Fund was transferred to:

options.A: The Depreciation Reserve Fund of the Railways
options.B: The Capital Fund of the Railways
options.C: The Railway Safety Fund
options.D: The general revenues of the Government of India

q: The National Small Savings Fund, maintained in the Public Account of India for the collections under the small savings schemes, was established with effect from:

options.A: 1 April 1991
options.B: 1 April 1999
options.C: 1 April 2004
options.D: 1 April 2016

q: The Reserve Bank of India makes a Ways and Means Advance to the Government to tide over a temporary mismatch between receipts and payments. Under Section 17(5) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, such an advance is repayable:

options.A: Within thirty days of the advance
options.B: Within one year of the advance
options.C: Not later than three months from the date of making the advance
options.D: At any time on demand by the Reserve Bank

q: The present system of Ways and Means Advances for the Central Government, introduced with effect from 1 April 1997, replaced the earlier system of:

options.A: Cash Management Bills
options.B: Ad hoc Treasury Bills
options.C: Dated Government securities
options.D: Market Stabilisation Scheme securities

q: The Railway Convention Committee reviews the financial relationship between the Railways and General Finances. The first such Committee after Independence was constituted in the year:
The Railway Convention Committee, an ad hoc Parliamentary committee, is constituted:

options.A: By the President under Article 263 of the Constitution
options.B: By the Railway Board through an office order
options.C: On a resolution adopted by the Lok Sabha and concurred in by the Rajya Sabha
options.D: By the Finance Commission along with its report

q: The Estimates Committee of Parliament, which examines the estimates of the Ministries, consists of:

options.A: 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha
options.B: 15 members, all from the Rajya Sabha
options.C: 22 members drawn from both Houses of Parliament
options.D: 45 members drawn from both Houses of Parliament

q: When the Public Accounts Committee is reconstituted, its members from the two Houses of Parliament come to the Committee:

options.A: By nomination by the Speaker and the Chairman respectively
options.B: By election in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote
options.C: By nomination by the Finance Minister
options.D: By election by a simple majority vote in each House

q: A proposal is made to include the following person in the Public Accounts Committee. Which of them cannot be a member of the Committee?

options.A: A member of the Rajya Sabha
options.B: A member belonging to an Opposition party in the Lok Sabha
options.C: A member who is also a member of the Estimates Committee
options.D: A Minister in the Council of Ministers
